verdict.rationale: Angular's own docs say apps are "organized yet modular thanks to Angular components and dependency injection" (angular-docs-2), and first-party modules work together across the platform (angular-docs-3). Community reports back this up: encapsulated, reusable components without dependency hell (angular-comm-2), built-in dependency injection (angular-comm-15), and modular code via @Input/@Output (angular-comm-1). Older AngularJS-era complaints about the provider docs and module namespacing are general criticism, not a concrete contradiction of modern Angular's DI. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the DI and provider system (the only first-party evidence is a marketing tagline), and hands-on evidence of DI scoping and hierarchical injectors in current Angular.
